My short list:

  1. Shovel Knight - a cross between Megaman and Castlevania and Duck Tales, very unique with lots of style and challenge.

  2. Axiom Verge - the discount Metroid look held me back for a while, but I finally dived in and it definitely scratches the itch.

  3. Braid - Say what you will about JBlow's politics, it's a quality game. Pretty dastardly puzzle platformer.

  4. VVVVVV - slippery controls but once you master them you feel like a badass. I love that there are no gates and you can do any level you want at any time.

  5. Cave Story - fantastic story, controls are a little floaty but it ties together a platform shooter with a non-one-hit-kill overhead shooter by joining your weapons strength to taking damage. Top notch and I believe it's still free on PC.

  6. Sufferer - a cute Zelda game that's relatively obscure by Fox Eye. All their games are pretty quality, but Sufferer is hard without being too punishing like Holdover or Sacrifice. Warning that all their games have to do with water and drowning and feature girls in tight swimsuits that can get torn and have them run around naked, but I assure you they are legitimate games and not just porn games. Games are free with some special editions available for pay but you might want to bring a translator to navigate the site (most are dual language).

My current tastes are roleplaying games, first person shooters, and puzzle games. But as for the first two I really can't find any amazing games in that vein. So my puzzler suggestions are pretty tough:

English Country Tune (3D grid-based game where the game goes into many variations. Control a 'thing' (a square, a beam, etc) and push other 'things' around (spheres that copy gravity))

Snakebird (2D grid-based game, using 'Snake''s mechanics, from a side view instead of top down, collecting fruits and leaving the exit)

-- Optimization puzzlers --
This genre is too niche unfortunately so many do not even realize these sorts of things exist. Basically puzzle games with lots of replay value because your solution isn't always the best one.

SpaceChem (2D optimization puzzler about pseudo-chemistry where you bond atoms to make new ones, has many variations on the idea as well. No chemistry knowledge is needed at all.)

Infinifactory (3D optimization puzzler that uses the same base idea of SpaceChem, but uses variations in very different ways (involved with pushing blocks and lifting them instead). Actually has a level editor)

Great Permutator (2D opt-puzzler, change the order and color of blocks to move them to different locations. A bit more limited compared to the other games here, and has a pretty consistent level scheme while still keeping each level unique)

LogicBox (not on Steam) (2D opt-puzzler, has no timing restrictions, uses 'boxes' that change the properties of a symbol sequence to create new boxes with increasing capabilities. Not as difficult as the other games that surround it, but can be thanks to its replay value.)

Prelogate (2D opt-puzzler, has no timing restrictions, uses logic gates to redirect and change the colors of lasers to get them in the right order. I say 2D in jest because stupidly, using 2D mode in the puzzles where blocks are elevated hide the distinction between elevated and non-elevated blocks. Loosely related with programming unlike the other games.)
